t: When a product is designed with a 'limited premium payment term' shorter than the policy term, the effect on the annual premium compared to a regular premium version of the same benefits is that it is:
o: Higher, because the same benefit value must be recovered over fewer premiums
Lower, because fewer premiums are paid
The same, because the sum assured is unchanged
Lower, because reserves build up faster
e: The present value of benefits is unchanged, but the premium annuity factor is smaller for a shorter payment term, so each premium must be larger.

t: Under the Use and File procedure for life products, which of the following is TRUE?
o: The insurer may launch the product immediately after filing, provided it complies with regulations and has been approved by the Product Management Committee
IRDAI must issue a unique identification number before any sale
The product must be reviewed by an external actuary before filing
Only products with sum assured below ₹10 lakh qualify
e: Use and File lets insurers launch compliant products after internal governance approval and filing; IRDAI can still direct modification or withdrawal later. The other conditions are not part of the procedure.

t: A product review under IRDAI guidelines must be carried out by the insurer at least:
o: Annually, with the Appointed Actuary assessing whether pricing remains appropriate
Every month
Every ten years
Only when IRDAI directs
e: Insurers must review product performance regularly (at least annually) against pricing assumptions, and withdraw or re-file products whose experience or regulatory position has changed.

t: Under Section 45 of the Insurance Act, 1938 (as amended in 2015), a life policy cannot be called in question on any ground after the expiry of:
o: 2 years from the date of issue
3 years from the date of issue, revival or rider addition, whichever is later
5 years from the date of issue
1 year from the date of claim
e: Section 45 bars repudiation on any ground, including fraud, after three years from the date of issue, commencement of risk, revival or rider, whichever is latest. This affects pricing of early-duration claims risk.

t: An insurer launched a product priced with a margin that, on review, shows an actual IRR far below the hurdle rate. Under the 2024 Product Regulations the most appropriate action is to:
o: Continue selling until the regulator objects
Increase premiums on existing policies
Modify or withdraw the product following the Product Management Committee review and refiling norms
Reduce the guaranteed benefits on existing policies
e: Existing policies' terms cannot be changed unilaterally; the remedy is to modify the product for new sales (or withdraw it) following the PMC process and file the revised version.

t: Which of the following best explains why premiums for the same product vary by age at entry?
o: IRDAI prescribes age-based premium tables
Commission rates vary with age
Older customers have higher incomes
Mortality rates and the expected period of premium payment both change with age
e: Mortality rises with age, increasing the benefit cost, while the annuity factor over which premiums are spread falls; both push premiums up. Regulations do not prescribe rates.

t: A pricing actuary sets assumptions with reference to 'the insurer's own experience, where credible, otherwise industry or reinsurer data'. This principle is referred to as:
o: Prudence
Materiality
Relevance and credibility of data
Equity between generations
e: Assumptions should be based on relevant data that is sufficiently credible; where own data is thin, external data is used and adjusted. Prudence and materiality are separate principles.

t: Which of the following is the most appropriate target premium rate basis for a product sold predominantly through corporate agents (banks)?
o: Lower per-policy expense loading and lower lapse rates than agency channel, reflecting channel experience
Identical assumptions to the agency channel
Higher commission than any other channel
No expense loading because the bank bears all costs
e: Channel-specific experience (acquisition cost, persistency, average premium size) should be reflected in pricing. Banks typically have lower per-policy acquisition cost and better persistency than individual agents.

t: A term assurance block has 400 expected claims per year and the insurer uses full credibility at 1,600 claims with the square-root rule. If the insurer's own experience shows an A/E of 120% and industry data shows 100%, the credibility-weighted mortality adjustment is:
e: Z = √(400/1,600) = 0.5. Blended A/E = 0.5 × 120% + 0.5 × 100% = 110%. Partial credibility weights own experience against the broader base.

t: In a select-and-ultimate mortality table with a two-year select period, q[x]+1 denotes the mortality rate of a life:
o: Aged x+1 who was selected one year ago (duration 1)
Aged x who was selected one year ago
Aged x+1 in the ultimate section
Aged x at duration 2
e: The bracket indicates age at selection and the subscript the elapsed duration; q[x]+1 applies at age x+1, one year after selection. After the select period, ultimate rates q(x+2) apply.

t: For an endowment assurance with sum assured ₹10,00,000, the pricing basis gives A(x:n) = 0.45 and ä(x:n) = 12.5. The net annual premium is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Net premium = SA × A / ä = 10,00,000 × 0.45 / 12.5 = ₹36,000. This covers benefits only and has no loading for expenses or profit.

t: The 'mortality drag' or longevity risk is most significant for which of the following products?
o: Term assurance
Whole life assurance
Immediate life annuity
Endowment with short term
e: Longevity risk, the risk that annuitants live longer than assumed, directly increases annuity outgo. For assurance products, longer life reduces cost.

t: A non-par policy promises a guaranteed maturity benefit of ₹5,00,000 after 10 years for a single premium. If the insurer can earn 7% p.a. and ignores mortality and expenses, the single premium required is approximately:
e: Premium = 5,00,000 / (1.07)^10 = 5,00,000 / 1.96715 = ₹2,54,175. A lower earned rate would require a higher premium, illustrating interest rate sensitivity.

t: If a liability has a duration of 12 years and the backing assets a duration of 7 years, a fall in interest rates will:
o: Reduce the value of both equally
Increase the value of assets by more than liabilities, creating a surplus
Have no effect since both increase
Increase the value of liabilities by more than the value of assets, creating a deficit
e: Value sensitivity to interest rate changes is proportional to duration. With longer liability duration, liabilities rise more than assets when rates fall, so the insurer's position worsens.

t: Which of the following best describes 'reinvestment risk' for a life insurer?
o: The risk of equity market falls
The risk that cash flows from assets maturing before the liabilities will have to be reinvested at lower yields
The risk that a bond issuer defaults
The risk of policyholders surrendering to reinvest elsewhere
e: Reinvestment risk arises from mismatch when assets are shorter than liabilities. Default risk is credit risk and equity falls are market risk.

t: An insurer's expense analysis gives initial expenses of ₹2,500 per policy plus 10% of first-year premium, and renewal expenses of ₹400 per policy plus 2% of renewal premium. For a policy with annual premium ₹25,000, the expense in the first year and in each renewal year respectively are:
e: First year = 2,500 + 10% × 25,000 = ₹5,000. Renewal = 400 + 2% × 25,000 = ₹900 (before inflation). Mixed loadings of this type are standard in cash flow pricing.

t: A policy has an annual premium of ₹30,000. Initial expenses are ₹3,000 per policy plus commission of 20% of the first-year premium; renewal expenses are ₹250 per policy plus 3% of premium. The total expense and commission outgo in the first policy year is:
e: First-year outgo = 3,000 + 20% × 30,000 = 3,000 + 6,000 = ₹9,000. Renewal loadings (₹250 + 3% = ₹1,150) apply from the second year onwards, not in year 1.

t: An insurer pays agents' commission of 35% of first-year premium on a 15-year endowment. Which of the following statements about the effect on the product is correct?
o: Commission has no effect on profitability as it is passed to the policyholder
Commission reduces the reserve required
High first-year commission increases new business strain and lengthens the payback period
Commission affects only the renewal expense loading
e: First-year commission is a major initial outgo; it increases the capital needed at inception and delays recovery. It is not recoverable from the policyholder upfront under level premium designs.

t: Overhead expenses such as head office rent and senior management salaries are allocated to products in expense analysis because:
o: IRDAI mandates a fixed allocation rate
Premiums must recover all expenses, including those not directly attributable, for the business to be profitable
They are small and immaterial
They are recovered from shareholders
e: Indirect expenses must be covered by premium loadings using appropriate allocation keys (policies, premiums, staff numbers). Leaving them out would understate the gross premium.

t: An insurer's experience shows 12 deaths over an exposure of 4,000 life-years in a block of business. The crude mortality rate is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Crude rate = deaths / exposed to risk = 12 / 4,000 = 0.003. Exposure is measured in life-years, allowing for policies entering and leaving during the period.

t: Under the IRDAI Master Circular on life products (2024), the special surrender value is computed as the paid-up value discounted at a rate not exceeding:
o: The 10-year G-Sec yield plus 50 basis points
The 10-year G-Sec yield plus 200 basis points
8% per annum fixed
The pricing interest rate plus 100 basis points
e: The SSV must be at least the expected present value of the paid-up sum assured and accrued benefits, discounted at no more than the 10-year G-Sec yield plus 50 bps, making surrender values fairer to early exits.

t: A policy with sum assured ₹5,00,000 and a 20-year term lapses after 4 of 20 annual premiums. Its paid-up sum assured is ₹1,00,000, payable after 16 more years. Using a discount rate of 7.5% (10-year G-Sec plus 50 bps) and ignoring mortality, the special surrender value is approximately:
e: Paid-up SA = 5,00,000 × 4/20 = ₹1,00,000. SSV = 1,00,000 / (1.075)^16 = 1,00,000 / 3.1808 = ₹31,440. The 2024 Master Circular requires the SSV to be at least this discounted paid-up value.

t: Which of the following is most likely to reduce early lapses for a regular premium product?
o: Higher first-year commission
Shorter free look period
Need-based selling, premium affordability checks and persistency-linked distributor remuneration
Higher surrender charges
e: Lapses are driven by mis-selling and unaffordable premiums; aligning distributor incentives to persistency and ensuring suitability improve retention. Surrender charges penalise but do not address the cause.

t: A life insurer charges a 'modal loading' of 5% for monthly mode. If the annual premium is ₹24,000, the monthly premium is:
e: Monthly premium = 24,000 × 1.05 / 12 = ₹2,100. The loading compensates for loss of interest and higher collection cost when premiums are paid more frequently.

t: Under the cash flow method, premiums, benefits, expenses and reserves are projected year by year. Profit in year t is calculated as:
o: Premium − expenses − claims + investment income on (reserve b/f + premium − expenses) − increase in reserve
Premium − claims only
Premium × profit margin
Investment income − expenses
e: The profit vector is the net cash flow after allowing for interest earned and the change in reserves. Reserves transfer profit between years and determine the strain.

t: A customer aged 35 wants a long-term savings contract with a guaranteed minimum maturity amount plus a share in the insurer's investment performance, with returns smoothed over time. Which product best meets this need?
o: Participating endowment assurance
Unit linked endowment
Non-participating pure term plan
Immediate annuity
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). A participating endowment gives a guaranteed sum assured plus bonuses declared from smoothed surplus. A ULIP passes investment risk directly to the policyholder without smoothing, while term and annuity plans do not meet a savings need at age 35.

t: For an endowment of sum assured ₹8,00,000 for 10 years with A(x:10) = 0.60 and ä(x:10) = 8.0, a per-premium loading of 10% of gross premium and a per-policy loading of ₹500 p.a. are required. The gross annual premium is:
In the formula method, the net single premium for a pure endowment of ₹1,00,000 payable at the end of 10 years to a life aged 40 is computed using:
o: A(40:10) in full
The probability of surviving 10 years multiplied by v^10
q(40) only
e: Pure endowment value = 10p40 × v^10 × SA; only survival to the end of the term triggers payment. The full A(x:n) includes the death benefit component as well.

t: A regular premium product has PV of premiums ₹4,40,000 per policy and a target profit margin of 5% of premiums. The PV of profits required at the risk discount rate is:
e: Required PV of profit = 5% × 4,40,000 = ₹22,000. If the profit test yields less, the premium or product design must be revised.

t: Which of the following would, other things equal, reduce the IRR of a product?
o: Holding higher (more prudent) statutory reserves
Reducing first-year commission
Lowering the risk discount rate
Increasing the sum assured proportionately with premium
e: Higher reserves increase the initial capital strain and delay the release of profit, lowering the IRR. Reducing commission improves IRR; the RDR affects NPV but not IRR.

t: A new product's expected profit signature at an RDR of 11% gives NPV of ₹1,500 per policy, but sensitivity testing with mortality 10% heavier reduces NPV to −₹300. The actuary should most appropriately:
o: Launch the product unchanged since the base case is profitable
Increase mortality margins, review reinsurance or adjust the premium so that the product remains viable under plausible adverse scenarios
Reduce the risk discount rate until the stressed NPV is positive
Ignore the sensitivity since IRDAI does not require it
e: A product that becomes loss-making under a modest stress is vulnerable. Sensitivity results drive margin setting, reinsurance decisions and premium level; manipulating the RDR is not a solution.

t: Which profit criterion is most useful when comparing two products that require very different amounts of initial capital?
o: NPV of profits
Profit margin on premiums
IRR, read together with the capital at risk
Total undiscounted profit
e: IRR expresses return per unit of capital, so it is suitable for comparing products with different strain, though it must be read with the absolute capital requirement and the duration of the investment.

topic: Participating Business, Bonuses and Asset Shares
t: A policy of sum assured ₹4,00,000 has received simple reversionary bonuses of ₹45 per ₹1,000 sum assured for each of 10 years. The total vested bonus is:
e: Annual bonus = 45 × 400 = ₹18,000; over 10 years = ₹1,80,000. Simple reversionary bonus is calculated on the original sum assured only, not on bonuses already attached.

topic: Participating Business, Bonuses and Asset Shares
t: Smoothing of bonuses in a participating fund means that:
o: Bonus rates are kept constant from year to year by regulation
Bonuses are declared only at maturity
All surplus is distributed immediately as cash
The insurer holds back surplus in good years and releases it in poor years so that bonus rates change gradually
e: Smoothing reduces year-to-year volatility of policyholder returns, which is a key feature distinguishing par products from unit linked products. It requires an estate or bonus reserve.

t: In a life insurance contract, insurable interest must exist:
o: At the time of the claim only
At inception of the policy
Both at inception and at claim
At renewal each year
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Life: at inception only. Marine: at the time of loss. Fire and motor: at both inception and loss.

topic: Participating Business, Bonuses and Asset Shares
t: Which of the following statements about the 'interim bonus' is correct?
o: It is guaranteed for the whole policy term at the rate last declared
It is paid on claims arising between two valuation dates, for the period since the last bonus declaration
It is the same as a terminal bonus
It is payable only on surrender
e: Interim bonus compensates claimants whose policies exit before the next annual bonus declaration, at a rate announced in advance; it is not a guarantee for future years.

topic: Unit Linked, Non-Par and Annuity Products
t: A unit linked fund of ₹10,00,000 is charged a fund management charge at the maximum permitted rate of 1.35% per annum. The annual FMC deducted (before any growth) is:
e: FMC = 1.35% × 10,00,000 = ₹13,500 per annum, deducted daily in the NAV. IRDAI caps the FMC at 1.35% p.a. for linked funds.

topic: Unit Linked, Non-Par and Annuity Products
t: For a unit linked policy with a term of more than 10 years, IRDAI's cap on the net reduction in yield at maturity is:
o: 4.00% per annum
3.00% per annum
2.25% per annum
1.35% per annum
e: The RIY at maturity may not exceed 2.25% for terms above 10 years (3% for terms of 10 years or less), and must not exceed 4% from the 5th policy anniversary onwards. This limits total charges over the term.

topic: Unit Linked, Non-Par and Annuity Products
t: A ULIP illustrates a gross investment return of 8% and after all charges the policyholder's projected yield at maturity is 6.2%. The reduction in yield is:
e: RIY = gross yield − net yield = 8.0% − 6.2% = 1.8%, within the 2.25% cap for terms over 10 years. RIY measures the aggregate effect of all charges except mortality charges.

topic: Unit Linked, Non-Par and Annuity Products
t: A non-par guaranteed income plan sold today promises ₹1,00,000 per annum for 10 years starting after 10 years. The main risk to the insurer, and its mitigation, is:
o: Mortality risk, mitigated by reinsurance
Interest rate risk, mitigated by matching with long-dated bonds and possibly forward rate agreements
Lapse risk, mitigated by surrender charges
Expense risk, mitigated by commission reduction
e: The product is a long-dated interest guarantee; falling yields would make it loss-making. Insurers mitigate by asset-liability matching and hedging instruments such as FRAs.

t: An accidental death benefit rider with sum assured ₹10,00,000 is priced at an accident death rate of 0.0006 per annum with a 40% loading for expenses and profit. The annual rider premium is:
e: Risk premium = 10,00,000 × 0.0006 = ₹600; with 40% loading = 600 × 1.4 = ₹840. Rider premium must also satisfy the regulatory cap relative to the base premium.

t: In group insurance pricing, a 'free cover limit' is:
o: The maximum sum assured available to a member without individual medical underwriting
The portion of the premium paid by the employer
The minimum group size for a scheme
The reinsurance retention limit
e: Free cover limits allow cover up to a threshold without evidence of health, relying on the group's non-selective nature; cover above the limit is underwritten individually.

t: A life insurer's non-linked required solvency margin computed from the factor formula comes to ₹30 crore. Under Section 64VA of the Insurance Act, 1938, the required solvency margin it must actually hold is:
o: ₹30 crore
₹45 crore
₹100 crore
₹50 crore
e: Section 64VA prescribes a minimum RSM of ₹50 crore for a life insurer (₹100 crore for a reinsurer), so the higher of the computed amount and ₹50 crore applies.

t: Non-disclosure of a material fact by the proposer makes the contract:
o: Void ab initio
Voidable at the option of the insurer
Illegal
Automatically continued on revised terms
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Breach of utmost good faith renders the contract voidable, not void; the insurer may elect to avoid it (subject to Section 45 for life).

t: The available solvency margin of a life insurer is computed as:
o: Excess of the value of admissible assets over the value of liabilities (policyholders' and other liabilities)
Total assets minus total premiums
Share capital only
Mathematical reserves plus free reserves
e: ASM = admissible assets − liabilities, with certain inadmissible assets (e.g. intangibles, preliminary expenses) excluded. It is compared to RSM to obtain the solvency ratio.

t: A prudent valuation basis (with margins for adverse deviation) compared to the pricing basis will generally lead to:
o: Lower reserves and earlier emergence of profit
Higher reserves, greater new business strain and deferred emergence of profit
No change in reserves
Higher premiums
e: Valuation margins increase reserves relative to the premium basis, so more capital is locked in at inception and profit emerges later as the margins are released.

t: A life insurer has APE of ₹1,000 crore (regular premium ₹800 crore plus single premium ₹2,000 crore) and value of new business of ₹200 crore. Its VNB margin is:
e: APE = regular premium + 10% of single premium = 800 + 200 = ₹1,000 crore. VNB margin = 200 / 1,000 = 20%. It is the headline measure of new business profitability.

t: Which of the following is NOT a component of the adjusted net worth in an embedded value calculation?
o: Free surplus
Required capital
Shareholders' share of assets over liabilities, marked to market
Present value of future profits on in-force business
e: ANW comprises required capital and free surplus held in shareholder funds. PVFP belongs to the value of in-force business, the other component of EV.

t: Which reinsurance arrangement is most suitable for a new insurer launching a high sum assured term product with limited capital and no own mortality experience?
o: Catastrophe excess of loss only
No reinsurance until experience develops
Quota share with risk premium reinsurance and reinsurer support in pricing and underwriting
Financial reinsurance only
e: Quota share reduces exposure per policy and smooths results, and the reinsurer typically provides mortality rates and underwriting manuals, which is valuable where own data is absent.

t: An insurer's expense experience study shows actual renewal expenses of ₹340 per policy against ₹300 assumed in pricing. The expense A/E ratio and the pricing implication are:
o: 113%; renewal expense loadings should be reviewed upwards
88%; loadings can be reduced
113%; no action needed since expense is small
100%; experience matches
e: A/E = 340 / 300 = 1.133, i.e. 113%. Actual expenses exceed those priced for, eroding margins; the loading (and inflation assumption) should be revisited.
